subject: Cooking
title: Chilies: The Americas' Hottest Export
description: A short lesson to help you apply Chilies: The Americas' Hottest Export.

hook.text: Thai food is unimaginable without chilies. But chilies didn't reach Asia until the 1500s.

buildup.text: All chili peppers originated in Central and South America, cultivated for over 6,000 years.

discovery.text: Portuguese traders introduced chilies to India, Thailand, and China — adoption was almost instant.

twist.text: Within 50 years, chilies had become so integrated that Asian cuisines seemed to have always used them.

climax.text: Today, India and China are the world's largest chili producers — far exceeding the Americas.

punchline.text: Asia's most iconic flavor is an American immigrant.

quiz.question: Where did all chili peppers originally come from?

details.summary: Chili peppers, domesticated in Mexico 6,000 years ago, spread globally after Columbus and conquered every major cuisine within 200 years. From Thai curries to Indian vindaloo to Sichuan hotpot, chilies became essential despite being unknown outside the Americas before 1492.
details.whyItMatters: Chilies are the fastest-adopted food in human history. Their global conquest reveals how powerfully capsaicin engages the human brain's pain-pleasure system, creating addictive flavor profiles across cultures.
takeaways: Chilies spread from the Americas to every continent within 200 years
Capsaicin triggers pain receptors, causing endorphin release as reward
Thai, Indian, and Chinese cuisines all adopted chilies relatively recently

faq.question: How did chilies spread so rapidly across the world?
faq.answer: Portuguese traders brought chilies from Brazil to their colonies in Africa, India, and Southeast Asia during the 1500s. Chilies grew easily in tropical climates, were cheap to cultivate, and provided intense flavor.

faq.question: Why do humans enjoy the pain of eating spicy food?
faq.answer: Capsaicin activates pain receptors on the tongue. The brain responds with endorphin release as a defense mechanism, creating a natural high.
